Ukraine is producing an increasing number of Neptune missiles but still lags behind Russia in production scale, The Wall Street Journal reports. Oleh Korostelyov, general director of the Luch Design Bureau, told the publication that the enterprise is expected to produce hundreds of Neptune missiles in 2026, though fewer than 1,000. For comparison, Russia launched 873 cruise missiles and 606 ballistic missiles at Ukraine in the first seven months of this year alone. In addition to Neptune missiles, the Luch Design Bureau produces Palianytsia jet-powered drones. According to Korostelyov, the enterprise manufactures more than 1,000 of these drones annually. Development of the Neptune began in 2010, but funding for its serial production did not arrive until late 2020. Korostelyov said additional funding would allow the enterprise to significantly increase production. Another challenge is the need to disperse manufacturing facilities and protect them from Russian strikes. According to the WSJ, Ukraine’s defense industry, which has expanded rapidly since 2022, is approaching the limits of its current capacity. Further expansion will require substantial investment, new production facilities, and skilled personnel.
